To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the particle inertia and its finite size can be used to control the particle transport in chaotic flows.

1. the particle inertia effects may strongly influence the chaotic motion in open flows, 2. the chaotic motion may be suppressed by the particle inertia and 3. the chaotic motion of a small inertial particle may be suppressed by a simple geometric configuration in an open flow.

the inertial effects may strongly modify a chaotic flow, to the point that it may be turned into a non-chaotic flow, or even into an attractor in the configuration space; that this effect can be used to design simple geometric setups that can trap inertial particles; that the effect can be used as a tool to separate and trap different types of particles in a flow; and that this effect may have relevance to modeling biological pathogen transport.

the study of chaotic transport and mixing of inertial tracers in unsteady flows, and the development of a novel particle trapping technique.
the study of chaotic advection in the presence of inertial effects and the use of these effects to control particle motion.
the study of the transport properties of inertial particles in chaotic flows.

the inertial effects in the tracer advection are very important and may be used to design a particle separator.
